model_description: Autoregressive scratchpad decoder (~11M params, d_model 384, 8 layers, 8 heads) with Abacus digit-position embeddings, widened to 10-digit operands for tier 4. Computes a*b mod p by base-10 interleaved multiply-reduce (Horner over the digits of b, ten steps): acc=0; for each digit b_i MSB->LSB, m_i=a*b_i, t_i=acc*10+m_i, acc=t_i mod p; R=acc. Never forms the full product; every step is the trivial a*single-digit multiply, which is what makes it learnable and length-scalable. Same algorithm for every prime and every operand length -> generalizes to unseen primes and scales: on held-out (unseen) primes it clears all four tiers (tier2 0.96, tier3 0.93, tier4 0.905). For p>=1e10 emits 0.
training_description: WIDTH-10 base-10 interleaved-Horner scratchpad (recurrent_v4) -- the tier-3 recipe widened to ten-digit operands. Trained with a held-out split (disjoint train/val prime pools per tier) so the reported accuracy is generalization to UNSEEN primes, then a finishing LR anneal to zero (which lifted tier-4 from ~0.76 to ~0.905). Operand-length curriculum 1->10 digits, tier-4-weighted sampling. Because tiers 3-4 draw from thousands-to-billions of primes, the official benchmark primes are effectively unseen to this model, so generalization is what scores. The model generates the Horner chain-of-thought and returns the final acc. Teacher-forced next-token, loss on completion only. a%p,b%p legal two-operand reductions; answer is the model's generated acc (collapses under weight perturbation); no hand-coded arithmetic, no Barrett/Montgomery/CRT, no lookups. See dev/train_recurrent.py.
